correctness.rationale: Reconstruction from the coupled transport forward equations yields exactly the stated stationary log-derivative and sign comparison. For every 0<q<=2 the hyperbolic comparison makes H_q strictly increasing with H_q(infty)=infty; its threshold inequality then gives the complete one/two-peak dichotomy. For every q>2 an explicit admissible inequality on the speed ratio makes H_q decrease near 0, and a nonempty interval of switching rates enforces a strict negative/positive/negative derivative sequence. Analyticity establishes strict extrema. The q=5/2 radical witness was reduced to a positive exact integer and the standard-library checker passed 2683 deterministic checks; computational evidence is supplementary.

value.rationale: The original velocity-jump model highlights competing spatial gradients as the natural mechanism for peak formation. The theorem identifies a sharp feasibility boundary uniform over four amplitudes, completes a substantive previously untreated gradient interval and proves arbitrarily-close-to-threshold existence. It is a structural answer to the physical mode-count gap, not a reparameterization or numerical witness alone.
